name: card
description: Find, inspect and fix the learner's review cards and mistakes (card.py in the self-hosted mode), keeping each card's id, review history and scheduling. A card's front is its content (the answer, in the target language), its back its answer (the meaning, the prompt; its (…) is a note shown on the flashcard only). Read: find {text} (id, front or back match), show {card_id} (how the app asks and grades it, its problems and overlaps), overlaps {card_id?}. Write, with a reason, dry_run first: edit {card_id, front?, back?, note?, category?}; regrade {card_id, quality, date?} (a review graded wrong by the card's fault: SM-2 replayed); merge {card_id (kept), drop_id}; split {card_id, new_id, new_front, new_back, new_note?, front?, back?}; forgive {pattern_id, date?, answer?} (a mistake that was the item's fault). force only when a refusal says so. language: another language's cards.

card_id.description: The card (show, edit, regrade, split; overlaps: optional; merge: the card kept).

drop_id.description: merge: the card that goes (its whole item is kept inside card_id's).

text.description: find: what to look for in ids, fronts and backs.

limit.description: find: at most this many cards (default 20).

front.description: edit, merge, split: the new front; alternatives joined with " / ", optional words in (…).

back.description: edit, merge, split: the new back (the prompt; (…) is a note).

note.description: edit, merge, split: the back's note, replacing its (…); "" removes it.

quality.description: regrade: the quality a right answer gets on that variant.

date.description: regrade: the review's day (default the latest); forgive: the mistake's day (default its latest example's).

answer.description: forgive: the learner's answer, when the day has several examples.

reason.description: Why (kept with the change). Give it on every write.

dry_run.description: A write: show the result, change nothing.

force.description: Do it despite a refusal that says force (a front with nothing to type, a history changed by hand).

language.description: Another language's cards: a code ("it") or a name. Omit for the home language.
